title: openai-compat: tool_choice schema mapping and tool message formatting for function/tool calling
author: Diego Chen
body: Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling with updated OpenAI semantics around tool_choice, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting. This PR clarifies how we choose between multiple tool variants, improves schema mapping to strongly typed outputs, and standardizes how tool invocation messages are serialized into the user-visible conversation. Summary: Implemented three coordinated changes: 1) tool_choice semantics: when a model indicates a tool_choice, map the choice to the canonical tool id with a deterministic fallback order and expose metadata in the response envelope; 2) schema mapping: add a pluggable mapper that validates model-provided JSON against tool schemas (OpenAPI-like) and emits normalized outputs or structured validation errors; 3) tool message formatting: standardize the shape of tool messages (name, id, input_schema, raw_input, parsed_input, metadata) and update the OpenAI-compat response format so downstream SDKs can consume tool outputs with minimal parsing. Design notes: The compatibility layer now registers tool definitions provided by the user (via API or SDK) and computes a mapping table at route registration time. At inference time, if model returns tool_choice.name or tool_choice.index, we resolve to the best match using exact id -> alias -> fuzzy match on display_name, then fall back to the first registered compatible tool. Schema mapping is performed using the existing schema-validator util with two new modes: strict (reject on first validation error) and best-effort (attempt partial extraction and include validation details in the response). Tool messages are serialized as JSON strings on the transport, but the compatibility layer attaches a parsed_input object to the parsed response metadata. Compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compat clients. Default behavior preserves prior semantics (legacy_mode) unless route opts into new_schema_mapping and tool_choice_strict flags. SDKs (Python/TS/Go) will be updated in follow-up PRs to provide helpers for the new parsed_input and validation metadata. Files changed (high level): redwood-openai-compat/src/compat/tool_choice_resolver.ts - deterministic resolver + alias table; redwood-openai-compat/src/compat/schema_mapper.ts - schema validator wrapper and mapping modes; redwood-openai-compat/src/compat/message_formatter.ts - unified tool message shape; redwood-openai-compat/tests/tool_choice_tests.ts - unit tests for resolution logic; redwood-openai-compat/tests/schema_mapping_tests.ts - tests for strict and best-effort modes; redwood/docs/openai_compat/tool_calling.md - doc updates and migration guide; redwood-openai-compat/examples/tool-schema-mapping/ - small example harness demonstrating an external inventory lookup tool. Test plan: Unit tests cover resolver heuristics, schema mapping modes, and message formatting. Added integration harness that simulates model outputs with tool_choice.name and tool_choice.index variations and asserts correct resolution and validation metadata. CI runs include lint, unit-tests, and integration-harness on a small containerized runtime. Rollout plan: Feature gate behind route-level flags (new_schema_mapping, tool_choice_strict). Start with opt-in beta for customers using OpenAI-compat; migrate high-usage routes after 2 weeks of telemetry observation. Metrics added for: tool_choice_resolutions, schema_validation_failures, schema_best_effort_successes, and tool_message_parse_errors. Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the resolver heuristics (resolver.ts line comments) -- the algorithm aims for determinism to avoid flapping across retries. Schema mapping leverages our existing validator but introduces performance trade-offs documented in the PR; best-effort mode should be used sparingly for low-latency paths. Related: ENG-2213 implements server-side telemetry for tool calls; PM-78 tracks doc/messaging updates and SDK follow-ups.
commits: aa7b3e9: add tool_choice resolver and alias table (tool_choice_resolver.ts)
b3d9f2c: implement schema_mapper with strict and best-effort modes (schema_mapper.ts)
c4e8a01: unify tool message formatting and update transport serialization (message_formatter.ts)
e2a9c33: small lint/test fixes after CI
review_comments: Ava Martinez: Can we avoid a full schema validation on hot paths? Suggest adding cached validation fingerprints and short-circuit for frequently-seen schemas.
Diego Chen (author): Added a schema fingerprint cache and fast-path in schema_mapper.ts that only runs full validation when fingerprint mismatch or best-effort mode is disabled.
Samuel Lee: What happens when model returns an unknown tool name? We should surface a clear validation/choice error to the caller instead of silently choosing a fallback.
Diego Chen (author): Updated resolver to emit resolution_reason in response metadata and to include a resolution_error when fallback is used. Also added telemetry counter for unknown_tool_choices.
Priya Kapoor: Docs look good; please add migration note about SDK helpers coming in next release so customers know to wait for SDK updates before turning on strict mode.
Diego Chen (author): Added migration note in redwood/docs/openai_compat/tool_calling.md and flagged the route gate as opt-in.
release_notes:
- Add deterministic tool_choice resolver with alias and fuzzy matching fallback.
- Add schema_mapper with strict and best-effort modes for mapping model JSON outputs to tool schemas.
- Standardize tool message formatting and expose parsed_input + validation metadata in OpenAI-compat responses.
- Route-level feature flags: new_schema_mapping, tool_choice_strict (opt-in).
discussion_threads: Design thread: resolver heuristics rationale and deterministic ordering (see comment chain)
Performance thread: schema validation cache and fast-path trade-offs
SDK follow-up: helpers to read parsed_input and validation metadata
notes: This PR intentionally leaves default behavior unchanged unless routes opt-in. Follow-up PRs will update SDKs and add experiments to migrate high-volume routes.
